prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Pleasanton CA for a checkup and cleaning?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what matters most to you (insurance, distance, child care, anxiety, language, hours). I can’t name one universal winner, but I can help find the best dentist in Pleasanton for your checkup and cleaning. Quick options:

1) Quick questions so I can recommend specific practices
- What is your ZIP code or neighborhood in Pleasanton?
- Do you have dental insurance or a particular plan/network?
- Any special needs (dental anxiety, children, seniors, medical issues, sedation)?
- Do you prefer a particular language, hours (evenings/weekends), or same-day availability?

2) How to pick a great dentist for a checkup & cleaning (fast checklist)
- Look for 4.5+ star ratings and many recent reviews on Google/Yelp/Healthgrades/Zocdoc.
- Verify they’re licensed (California Dental Board) and look for DDS/DMD credentials.
- Read reviews for hygienist skill, gentle cleanings, thorough exams, and good communication.
- Confirm they do a full exam (soft tissues/oral cancer screening), X-rays as needed, and discuss findings with you.
- Check infection-control practices and modern equipment (digital x-rays, ultrasonic scalers).
- Ask about first-visit process: length of cleaning, whether X‑rays are included, cancellation policy, and costs.
- If anxious, ask about nitrous oxide or other comfort options.

3) Questions to ask when booking
- “Do you accept my insurance?” (give plan details)
- “How long is a routine cleaning appointment and what is included?”
- “Do you perform oral cancer screening and digital x‑rays on new patients?”
- “Can I meet or request a specific hygienist?”
- “What do first-time patients typically pay out of pocket?”

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and insurance (or say “no insurance”) and I’ll shortlist 3–5 well-reviewed Pleasanton dentists (with contact links and why each is a good fit). Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
